name: Crissy Field
notes: Presidio of San Francisco: PPIE aviation / drill field on the 1912-15 fill (1915), Army air coast-defense station built 1919-21 on the old racetrack (accepted 24 Jun 1921; Wikipedia), grass field '5,000 x 400 ft sandy loam' (1937 Airports Directory); Air Corps squadrons to Hamilton Field 1936; paved Runway 6/24 c.1947-48 (aerials 7/1946, 8/1948), 2,610 ft (1960); fixed-wing flying ended 1974 (Campbell, Two Hours by Crow), helicopters later. Not in Overture: outline + runway pieces in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson (USGS San Francisco North 1946-photo sheet, 1956, 1968 PR; data/manual/airports/tools/crissy.py); runway removed 1999 for the restoration

name: Santa Rosa Naval Auxiliary Air Station
notes: NAAS Santa Rosa (southwest of the city, between Wright Rd, Finley Ave and Ludwig Ave): construction from Nov 1942, '7,000-ft hard-surface runway' in the 1944 Army / Navy directory, '2 concrete 7,000-ft runways, north / south and east / west' in the 1945 AAF directory; Navy OLF to 1947 and again 1951-52 (Korea), abandoned on the 1961 / 1966 charts, civil Santa Rosa Air Center (O01) from 1966-67, closed 1991 (Freeman). Not in Overture: runways, ramp, taxiways and outline traced from the USGS Sebastopol / Santa Rosa 1:24,000 sheets of 1954 (1952 photos, 'Naval Auxiliary Air Station (Inactive)') in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson (tools/newarea.py); the north half of the N-S runway, the west end of the E-W runway and the ramp still exist

name: Cotati Naval Outlying Landing Field
notes: NOLF Cotati (today's Rohnert Park, west of US-101 at the Expressway): built 1941-43 as an auxiliary air station (airfield on a 1942 aerial, on the Aug 1943 chart; '3,900-ft runway' 1944, field carrier landing practice on Runways 7/25 and 13/31), 'the field was closed in 1946' (Campbell via Freeman). The runways were a road-racing circuit and drag strip 1957-72 (Cotati Raceway) and were built over from 1973 (Rohnert Park Expressway 1971-73, mobile home park by 1977, shopping centres 1986). Runways traced from the USGS Cotati 1:24,000 sheet of 1954 (1952 photos, 'Cotati Naval Auxiliary Air Station (Inactive)'; still on the 1968 photorevision, gone on the 1980 one) with their own years (end 1973) in data/manual/airports_extra.geojson; the airfield outline closes 1946

name: Santa Cruz Sky Park
notes: Scotts Valley: 'Sky Park Airport began operation in 1947 as a privately-owned field built by Jack & Lola Graham' (county airport chronology via Freeman), 2,100-ft runway; city of Santa Cruz airport after Capitola closed (1954); realigned, longer runway built c.1968 ('the 1968 USGS topo map depicted the original runway ... along with the realigned runway which replaced it'); 'Skypark closed in January 1983'. Traced from the USGS Felton 1:24,000 sheets (1953 photos; 1980 photorevision; 1991 'Landing Strip (Abandoned)') in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson

name: Santa Cruz-Capitola Airport
notes: the bluff between Capitola and New Brighton Beach (today's Cliffwood Heights streets): flying field on a 1925 aerial (start ESTIMATED from it), Santa Cruz's civil airport from 1934, 'abandoned in September 1954' when the operators moved to Sky Park (Freeman); streets on the 1968 photorevision. Field outline and the two turf runways traced from the USGS Soquel 1:24,000 sheet of 1954 (1952 photos) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson

name: Rio Vista Airport (original)
notes: north edge of Rio Vista at St Francis Way / Airport Rd: 'in 1949 crop duster Ira Skip Seiden cut a single runway into the dirt just to the north of Rio Vista' (Campbell via Freeman; on the Aug 1948 chart), municipal airport 'established in 1953' (1988 county plan), 2,500-ft Runway 7/25 + 1,700-ft 14/32 in the 1960 Jeppesen manual, replaced by today's airport 2 miles north, built 1993-95 (see Rio Vista Municipal Airport). Traced from the USGS Rio Vista 1:24,000 sheets (1949 photos; 1974 photos) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson; hangars and some pavement remain (not modelled after 1995)

name: Antioch Airport
notes: Lone Tree Way east of Empire Ave (today Deer Valley High School and houses): 'Orville Prevost opened an airport in 1946', gravel runway 2,200 ft, 'paved out to 2,480 ft' in 1949, 'the field closed in 1989' (Campbell via Freeman; not on the Aug 1946 chart, on the Feb 1947 one). Runway and property outline traced from the USGS Antioch South 1:24,000 sheet of 1953 (1949 photos; coarse, +-12 m) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson

name: Petaluma Sky Ranch Airport
notes: East Washington St (today's Sky Ranch Drive houses, directly south-west of the municipal airport): not on the Feb 1949 chart, on the Sep 1949 one; Justman Flying Service; 2,100-ft runway, paved later; 'the Sky Ranch was dismantled, and Petaluma Municipal Airport opened in 1985' (Freeman) - the FAA activation 06/1949 of O69 is the Sky Ranch's. Traced from the USGS Petaluma River 1:24,000 sheets (1952 photos; 1980 photorevision) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson. Earlier Petaluma fields (1915 flights; Petaluma Airport / Skyways 1946- on the north-west side; Buck / Doolittle, Justman, Oak View) not modelled

name: Vallejo Sky Harbor
notes: north Vallejo west of Broadway (SR-29) at today's Meadows Dr: 'established Vallejo Sky Harbor Airport on 2/9/46', 2,500-ft unpaved runway (1948 chart), 'the field closed in 1953' (Freeman; off the Mar 1953 chart; houses on its south-east part on a 1957 aerial). Four strips traced from the USGS Cuttings Wharf 1:24,000 sheet of 1949 (1948 photos) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson. The pre-war Vallejo (Mini) Airport 1.5 km south (1929-c.1944, only a boundary symbol on the 1:62,500 sheet) is not modelled

name: Calistoga Airpark
notes: Calistoga Airpark / Gliderport on Lincoln Ave east of the town: not on the Feb 1947 chart, on the Aug 1947 one, 2,200-ft unpaved runway (1948), paved by 1957; glider field (Calistoga Soaring Center); 'closed in December 1998 & all flying ceased' (Campbell via Freeman). Runway traced from the USGS Calistoga 1:24,000 sheet of 1958 (1957 photos; same on the 1980 photorevision: 665 m - the '2,800-ft' of the directories is not drawn) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson

name: Morgan Hill Airport
notes: Cochrane Rd east of US-101 (Morgan Hill Airmen Landing Strip, later Sutter Airfield, Q99): 'Valley Airport' with unpaved 1,700-ft runways in the 1947 Haire directory (start ESTIMATED from it; first on the Sep 1950 chart), 2,400-ft unpaved runway; abandoned on the 1981 sectional, last photo 1980 (Freeman) - end ESTIMATED. Traced from the USGS Morgan Hill 1:24,000 sheets (1953 photos; 1973 photorevision) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson

name: Watsonville Airport (original)
notes: San Andreas Rd / Salinas Rd junction south-west of Watsonville (Monterey County): 'Watsonville Airport Incorporated was formed in 1930', dedicated 1931 (Governor Rolph), three runways on a 1938 aerial; 'leased by the Navy in 1942' for blimps from Moffett Field (NAAF Watsonville: the runways filled in with one asphalt mat and mooring circles on a 1943 aerial); still on the Mar 1945 chart beside the new airport, 'Old Airport' on a 1950 road map (Freeman) - end ESTIMATED. Runways traced from the USGS Capitola 1:62,500 sheet of 1940 (1938 photos; +-30 m) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson; the 1943 blimp mat is not modelled

name: Vaca-Dixon Airport
notes: south-east side of I-80 at Midway Rd / Meridian Rd (next to the Vaca Valley Raceway): 'opening in 1947' with dirt runways (Campbell via Freeman; on the Feb 1948 chart), 'Airport Abandoned' on the 1973 photorevision but in use again for ultralights and gliders: 'when the gliders moved out on 12/1/93, the airport certificate was pulled' ('other sources reported ... closed in 1995'). Two runways traced from the USGS Allendale 1:24,000 sheet of 1953 (1949 photos; coarse, +-12 m) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson

name: Vacaville Gliderport
notes: Lagoon Valley, east side of I-80 at Lagoon Valley Rd (Shady Grove / Vacaville Airport, VCV; not the Nut Tree Airport 6 km north-east): not on the 1951 sheet or the Oct 1956 chart, on the 1957 chart, 2,000-ft Runway 2/20 paved by 1962, 'the field was closed on 9/25/91' (Campbell via Freeman). Runway traced from the USGS Fairfield North 1:24,000 photorevisions of 1968 and 1980 (coarse, +-15 m) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson

name: Knights Airport
notes: Vallejo, on the Napa River flat north-west of Sears Point Rd (SR-37) at Sacramento St (Knights Airport / Stan's Airpark): a 1935 photo is the earliest record (start ESTIMATED from it; on the May 1936 chart), closed during the war (off the charts Aug 1943 - Feb 1946), 2,300-ft unpaved runway in 1948; 'by 1954 the runways were deteriorating & the Napa County Airport was a better choice so this field was closed' (Campbell via Freeman). Strips traced from the USGS Cuttings Wharf 1:24,000 sheet of 1949 (1948 photos) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson; the pre-war strips are not mapped (the field is airfield grass from 1935, the traced strips from 1946)

name: Benicia Airport
notes: west edge of Benicia between Benicia Rd and the Southampton Bay marsh (Benicia Airport / Air Harbor; I-780 runs over it): 'in 1946, when the runway was opened' (Campbell via Freeman; not on the 1946 chart, on the 1948 one), 2,400-ft unpaved runway; last on the Sep 1957 chart, off the Apr 1958 one -> closed 1957-58 (still labelled on the 1958-photo USGS sheet, abandoned on a 1965 aerial). Two strips traced from the USGS Benicia 1:24,000 sheet of 1950 (1948 photos) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson

name: Santa Rosa Coddingtown Airport
notes: north-west Santa Rosa between Piner Rd and Guerneville Rd, west of today's Coddingtown (Santa Rosa Metropolitan / Coddingtown Airport): 'built off of Piner Road in 1960' (Sonoma County Historical Society via Freeman), dedicated 1960, 3,050-ft paved Runway 16/34 (1967-68); sold 1971 - 'the main portion of the field became a parking lot for the buses of the Golden Gate Transit District', 'closed by 1972' (a heliport stayed into the 1980s). Runway traced from the 1968 photorevision of the USGS Santa Rosa 1:24,000 sheet (920 m) in data/manual/airports_extra*.geojson. The earlier fields on the same ground (Santa Rosa Municipal / Steiner Field 1929-, Santa Rosa Airpark c.1953) are not modelled: the 1:62,500 sheet of 1944 shows only a boundary, the 1954 sheet nothing

name: Capell Valley Airport

name: Monterey Bay Academy Airport
